title: Will the polysilicon Section 232 drive upstream solar manufacturing to the US?
gist: Wood Mackenzie expects the Section 232 polysilicon measures, effective Dec. 4, 2026, to lift US utility-scale module prices above $0.40/W, near 2022 highs, and raise utility-scale system costs 20%. It argues the policy mainly rewards already-integrated cell-to-module makers rather than spurring new polysilicon and wafer capacity.

insights.claim: Trump signed a Section 232 proclamation on polysilicon and derivatives on Aug. 6, 2026 after a 13-month Commerce investigation, with measures effective Dec. 4, 2026.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Sets the timeline for US solar cost resets and procurement decisions.

insights.claim: Unlike targeted AD/CVD cases, Section 232 applies globally, closing the ability to dodge duties by shifting production between countries.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Removes the Southeast Asia-style country-hopping arbitrage that shaped past solar sourcing.
insights.quote: Section 232 applies globally - closing off suppliers' ability to dodge duties by shifting production between countries.

insights.claim: The measures set minimum import prices at every stage of the module value chain plus a 15% tariff on polysilicon derivatives, with onshoring relief only for polysilicon, ingot, wafer or cell investment, not module-only.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Module-only assemblers are structurally excluded from relief; implementation details remain unresolved.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie expects utility-scale module prices to rise above $0.40/W, back near the 2022 peak.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Raises US solar project costs and PPA prices, a headwind to developers' returns and volumes.
insights.quote: We expect the tariffs to push utility-scale module prices above $0.40/W, back near their 2022 peak.

insights.claim: Full price impact will be delayed into 2027 because US inventory exceeds a year's installations, though suppliers raised prices $0.01-0.02/W immediately after the proclamation.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Inventory buffers delay the pain, so watch 2027 procurement and pricing.

insights.claim: Higher module prices raise modeled C&I system costs by 11% and utility-scale system costs by 20%, which may push projects to be delayed, renegotiated or cancelled.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Expect PPA price increases and pipeline attrition for US solar developers.

insights.claim: Section 232 improves economics for partially integrated manufacturing, with wafer-to-module producers lowest cost while 45X credits remain, and cell-to-module producers able to land below the $0.38/W module MIP.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Integrated cell-and-module makers are the near-term beneficiaries.

insights.claim: The polysilicon and wafer minimum import price is still not enough to offset the cost of new domestic capacity, given long timelines, high capital costs and policy uncertainty.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Do not underwrite new US polysilicon or wafer capacity from this tariff alone.
insights.quote: the new minimum import price for polysilicon and wafers still isn't enough to offset the cost of building new domestic capacity

insights.claim: Only 6.4 GW of integrated cell-and-module capacity is operational in the US and no domestic manufacturer has enough cell capacity for its own module demand, so even integrated players must keep importing components.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Even winners bear rising import costs near term.

insights.claim: Module-only assemblers, ineligible for onshoring relief and facing higher imported cell costs, will struggle to compete.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Avoid or short pure assembly models in the US.

insights.claim: The eventual phase-down of 45X manufacturing credits works against greenfield investment in upstream segments.
insights.speaker: Elissa Pierce
insights.so_what: Policy sunset risk weighs on US upstream solar capex.
